newsitem.title: USA: Oregon's House passes transportation tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Oregon's House passes transportation tax bill.

text.p: Oregon's House passed a revised version of its earlier transportation tax bill on Thursday, calling for a six cent per gallon tax increase on gasoline and higher vehicle registration fees to fund road construction in the state.
The measure, passed 41-19 by the House, now needs approval by the state Senate.
In June, Oregon's Senate first watered down the House's original plan, which called for a nine cent per gallon tax over three years, and then rejected the measure entirely.

The state's trucking industry strongly opposes the bill. Governor John Kitzhaber is a strong supporter of the transportation tax measure and has indicated he might call a special session if lawmakers cannot send the bill to him soon.

The state's new fiscal year began July 1 and lawmakers have been working late into the night for the past week to try to finish this year's session. The Oregon legislature meets every other year and there is a House move to put a ballot measure on the 1998 ballot asking voters to approve annual sessions.
House members have argued that the state's budget has grown so much it is impossible to complete work on funding with only biannual sessions.
Missing from the revised bill is a controversial telephone tax that would have funded transportation for the disabled and elderly.

The new bill has a safety fund for senior and disabled transportation to be paid for from income taxes expected from construction projects supported by the gas tax increase. During the first six years the gas tax is expected to raise $1.3 billion.
